extracted.intended_audience: graduate students, literary critics, and creative writers interested in narratology and narrative technique
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and production guidance for narrative time, frequency, and mood: how tense/aspect, frequency (iterative vs singulative), temporal markers, memory, and narrative distance/perspective shape a text's temporal and modal stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative versus singulative (frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish iterative (habitual, repeated) sections from singulative (single-event) sections; passages may begin iterative and continue singulative or vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives many Proustian examples where an iterative beginning is followed by a singulative continuation; such abrupt switches can produce 'irreducible unrealism' if their temporal standing is not indicated. If a singulative is meant to belong to a series, include a temporal marker (e.g., 'once' / 'the very first time') to locate it; absence of such markers can create a floating, disconcerting impression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explicit temporal indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporal markers (e.g., 'the first of these days', 'for a long time') assign iterative or singulative values and place events in a series or plateau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding a small explicit marker can restore chronological order and remove ambiguity; conversely omitting them can be a deliberate device to create masking or floating effects. Example: 'For a long time' assigns iterative value and stabilizes the following passage as iterative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral sections that mask aspect changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections inserted between iterative and singulative portions whose aspect is indeterminate and which serve to hide aspectual change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three kinds are identified: (1) discursive excursuses in the present tense (extranarrative), (2) abruptive dialogue without a declarative verb, and (3) ambiguous imperfects (mixed/indeterminate). Authors may use these to smooth transitions so readers do not notice the change of aspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discursive excursuses in present tense (extranarrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long present-tense digressions interposed between different aspectual sections, having extranarrative status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clearly separate planes (narrative vs commentary) and can intentionally interrupt aspectual continuity; use when you want an explicit, non-diegetic pause or commentary rather than to disguise aspect change within the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abruptive dialogue (dialogue without declarative verbs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue restricted to rejoinders lacking declarative verbs (Fontanier's 'abruptioll'), which by definition has no determination of aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abruptive dialogue functions as a neutral carrier between iterative and singulative passages; because it lacks verbs and explicit aspect, it does not fix temporal relations and thus can mask transitions. Use deliberately to displace aspectual anchoring; avoid it if clear temporal sequencing is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous imperfects (mixed/indeterminate aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interposing imperfect-verb forms whose aspectual value remains indeterminate to create an ambiguous or neutral section between iterative and singulative passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subtle technique sustains irresoluteness across lines or paragraphs (examples from Un amour de Swann). Use to modulate temporal stance without explicit markers; be aware it can produce a sense of floating or unresolved temporality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative syllepsis (frequency-condensing device)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative operation that synthesizes several 'similar' events into one, thus abolishing their succession and eliminating intervening time intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative syllepsis affects frequency, sequence, and duration simultaneously (condenses events into a single narrative); use to create plateaux of repetition or to mask diachronic movement. It is a powerful device for producing static or epochal effects in memory-driven narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation of scenes and ellipses (distortion of duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques that alternate between fully narrated scenes and temporal ellipses, thereby distorting perceived duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operation governs how long events are stretched or contracted in narrative time; use large ellipses to compress long spans, scenes to expand moments. Proust exploits these to make the flight of time perceptible or to create musical tempo effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analepsis often realized as summary (sequence-duration link)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analepsis (flashback) frequently takes the form of summary, linking sequence (order) with duration/speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that summary reduces duration and can be used to reframe sequence; summaries often make use of iterative forms. Choosing summary vs full-scene analepsis changes narrative tempo and perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy of temporal distortions: interpolations, distortions, condensations
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify temporal anomalies according to the aspect they affect: interpolations (order/anachrony), distortions (duration), condensations (frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy to analyze or design narrative time: e.g., 'interpolations' mix epochs (Balzac example), 'condensations' collapse repeated events, and 'distortions' stretch or compress durations. Recognize which operation you are performing to control reader effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between narrative temporality and story temporality
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize a narrative's temporal stance by considering the relationships it establishes between the temporality of its discourse (narrative time) and that of the story it tells (diegetic time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One must consider order, duration, and frequency together; memory-driven narration often produces iteration and anachrony, while other narrating positions may reassert chronological succession. Analyses/choices should account for all these relations simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporality of narrating (narrating time) as distinct factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The temporal demands or impatience of the act of narrating itself can govern narrative distortions (e.g., the narrator may compress or load final scenes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize narrating time as a force distinct from story time and narrative time; it can produce enormous ellipses or 'monstrous scenes' and thus shapes final structure and pacing. Design narrator's temporality consciously when structuring an account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic justifications vs compositional choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may rationalize temporal anomalies by appeal to 'telling things as they were lived' or 'as they were recalled'; such rationalizations coexist with compositional decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically distinguish between an artist's post-hoc realistic/psychological justification and the compositional/aesthetic function those devices serve. Do not accept rationalizations uncritically; instead, examine how the technique functions aesthetically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory as compositional link (use of involuntary memory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use phenomena of memory (especially involuntary memory) as significant links to pass from one plane to another, as compositional devices rather than mere content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proust uses memory-events (e.g., the madeleine) to create transitions and to justify anachronies; treat memory as structural glue that can create meaningful joins between fragments. Using memory as direct compositional technique can legitimize sudden transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempo modulation and musical analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat variations in narrative tempo as musical modulation (shifts of tempo/tonality) rather than merely dramatic functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proust 'fashions almost a poetic equivalent of the chromaticism of Tristan' by exploiting tense/aspect ambiguity for harmonic subtlety. Use tempo shifts for aesthetic effect—to modulate feeling, intensity, or to simulate memory's elasticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative mood: distance and perspective as modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend grammatical 'mood' metaphorically: narrative mood regulates 'distance' (degree of affirmation/mediation) and 'perspective' (point of view/participant vision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use variations in how much and how directly information is reported to control reader distance; choose whether narrative is more diegetic (mediated) or mimetic (immediate) depending on desired closeness and authority of the tale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diegesis (pure narrative) versus mimesis (imitation/showing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diegesis (pure narrative, mediated report) is more distant and condensed; mimesis (imitation, direct representation) is more immediate and 'showing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plato's distinction (and its later Anglophone 'showing' vs 'telling') affects how direct characters' speech and actions are presented. Choose diegetic mediation for condensation or analytical distance, mimesis for immediacy and vivid scene presentation. Beware of ideological overvaluation of 'showing'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of affirmation via mood forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammatical moods (conditional, infinitive, subjunctive) express degrees of affirmation and points of view, and thus shape narrative information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modal verb forms can signal uncertainty, indirectness, or adopted participant perspectives; use them to calibrate how strongly the narrator asserts events or adopts a character's vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding naive valorization of 'showing' over 'telling'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'showing' vs 'telling' normative opposition is historically contingent and analytically simplistic; both mimesis and diegesis have distinctive functions (indirection, condensation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat showing as an absolute aesthetic good; analyze whether condensation, indirection, or mediation better serves the narrative effect. Wayne Booth's critique is cited to caution ideological readings.
